Killings of Indigenous People Map

Indigenous people killed, attacked, threatened, disappeared and massacred across the world, case by case, from colonial frontiers to today, beside the land and environmental defenders killed and the land conflicts of rural Brazil. Each case is at the place its source gives, with the source's own record in its box.

Time

Fromto

Records with no year are always shown. Each row's year is the source's: the date of the killing or event, or the year of the table or report that lists the case. Each layer's Details button opens what it is, where it comes from, and menus to colour its dots by one of its fields or keep only some of its records.

How dots are drawn

Filled dot: at the place the source gives (exact coordinates, or a town or municipality) Ring: the source names only a province, state or country; drawn at that area's middle Shaded country, state, province or municipality: darker for a higher figure

Where several records share one spot, they are drawn slightly apart in a small spiral so each can be clicked; each box says so. Where dots still overlap at a zoom, a click lists every one under it.
